title: What the Weaverbird makes

is_this_you.pressure: When the words jam, your hands start. By evening something is mended that nobody asked you to fix.
is_this_you.love: You say it with something you made, then hang on the branch and watch them look it over.
is_this_you.cost: Your own work looks brown to you within days, so you tear it down before anyone can call it old.

opener.text: A female weaver will usually accept only a green nest, one built within the last few days [v11]. The grass soon fades to brown, and once it does, that nest has had its chance [v11]. So the male keeps his hands moving. You were born a Virgo in a Rooster year, and you know this bird's hurry from the inside. Fresh work is how you say you are still here.

howto: Three parts. Pick one up and turn it over.

tabs.label: The nest
tabs.intro: Earth for the patience, Metal for the edge.

rows.text: Virgo is mutable Earth, ruled by Mercury, a sign known for technical skill [v1] [v2]. The Rooster is yin Metal, hardworking and resourceful [v3] [v4]. Virgo hides a feeling to keep the peace [v2], and the Rooster wants to be heard [v4]. You settle it with your hands. The thing you make does the talking.

A male baya cuts, weaves and knots strips of grass between 20 and 60 centimetres long, and one nest can take him up to 500 trips [v9]. For a weaver, the nest is the courtship display [v5]. Plenty of your feeling goes into the knots. The words turn up late, if at all.
Joinery and bookbinding reward your hands, and so does any bench where a thing is judged by whether it holds.

tabs.label: Starting over
tabs.intro: Twenty minutes to pull it down. Then the next strip.

rows.text: When a nest goes unchosen, the male tears it down in 20 to 30 minutes and builds a fresh one, sometimes right beneath the old [v11]. You have done both. You scrap the draft that sat too long, or you build the next one in its shadow.

Virgo can nitpick, and the Rooster can brag [v2] [v4]. So you say nothing about your work, or far too much. The Ghanaian poet Kofi Awoonor, writing in the Ewe dirge tradition, made the weaver bird an intruder that builds in a house where nobody invited it [v10]. Ask whose tree it is before you weave.

tabs.label: Who moves in
tabs.intro: Three who will live in what you build. One who will judge the weave.
tabs.love_lead: A baya female looks the nest over while it is still half-built, at the helmet stage, and signals whether she accepts it [v9]. You need a partner like her, who comes early, looks closely and says yes out loud. Three traditional pairings fit that bill.

easy.why: The Galápagos Tortoise (Taurus, Dragon year) is your secret friend, since the Dragon and the Rooster are a Six Harmonies pair, and Taurus is Earth like you [v3] [v1].
The Beaver (Virgo, Ox year) shares your trine of Rooster, Ox and Snake, and it builds under your own sign [v3].
The Shoebill (Capricorn, Ox year) comes in through the Ox as well, and Capricorn is the third Earth sign [v3] [v1].

hard.why: The Moon Jellyfish (Pisces, Rabbit year) is the hard one: the Rabbit clashes with the Rooster, and Pisces sits across the wheel from Virgo [v3] [v1].

story.text: A widespread folk belief in India says the baya sticks fireflies to its nest walls with mud, to light the chamber at night [v9]. The fireflies belong to the story. The mud is real, and may help steady the nest in wind [v9].

closing: Tie off the last strip while the grass is green. Then hang beneath it and let them look.
